html:
On 5 June 1981 the US Centers for Disease Control reported five cases of a rare pneumonia in young gay men in Los Angeles. It was the first official notice of what became the AIDS epidemic.

More cases quickly appeared, in gay men, drug users, people with haemophilia and Haitian immigrants. The illness was named AIDS, acquired immune deficiency syndrome, in 1982. In 1983 French scientists at the Pasteur Institute, including Luc Montagnier, found the virus that causes it, later called HIV.

The virus had in fact been spreading quietly for decades, from Central Africa and through the Caribbean, as the HIV reaches the Americas item shows. Once named, it became a global epidemic.

In the United States, fear and stigma were strong, and many felt the government of Ronald Reagan was slow to act. Activist groups such as ACT UP pushed for faster drug trials. The first drug, AZT, came in 1987, and combination therapy from 1996 turned HIV from a death sentence into a long term illness for those who could get treatment. More than 700,000 Americans have died of AIDS.
sum: On 5 June 1981 the US Centers for Disease Control reported five cases of a rare pneumonia in young gay men in Los Angeles. It was the first official notice of what became the AIDS epidemic.
